newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end lower, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end lower, led by banks.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed lower for the second consecutive session in trading that saw leading bank shares, including Banco de Bogota, dip sharply.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 1.07 percent to end at 18,423.53 on a trading volume of about 1.8 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB index fell 0.99 percent, meanwhile, ending the week at 1,213 on volume of about 1.6 billion pesos.
"The market is undergoing a strong correction and it had no strength today, especially given the absence of buyers," one Bogota-based broker said of the day's broad-based selling.

Banco de Bogota, the country's third leading bank and flagship of the Luis Carlos Sarmiento conglomerate, led the day's losers. It shed 5.63 percent in Bogota to close at 6,700 pesos per share and dropped 4.96 percent in Medellin.
Banco de Colombia, the country's No. 2 bank, fell 2.16 percent in Bogota, where it ended at 406 pesos per share.

The only bank that managed to buck the downward trend was blue-chip Banco Ganadero, which gained 1.25 percent in Bogota to close at 322 pesos per share. It added 2.54 percent in Medellin, where it settled at 323 pesos a share.
